clue.text: Felt middle of the long rope drag

indicators.note: the middle of a run of words is where the letters are found, tucked inside the long rope drag

explanation.surface: Someone feels the strain in the middle of a long tug-of-war rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' points inside the phrase: lonG ROPE Drag.
explanation.definitionFit: To grope is to feel about blindly with the hands, so felt is its past tense synonym.

clue.text: Saying mince pie leads to little weight

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up finely, so the letters of pie are chopped and rearranged

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Eating a mince pie leads to putting on a little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of the pastry, but it is the anagram signal: PIE becomes EPI.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short witty remark, a pithy saying.

clue.text: What painters paint, and in a variety of places

indicators.note: a variety of arrangements suggests the letters of and plus places are mixed up

explanation.surface: Painters work in many locations, a simple observation about artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a variety of' mixes AND with PLACES to give the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of countryside scenery, a classic subject for artists.

clue.text: The army man sounds a bit of a nut

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for the army man is said out loud to give a different spelling

parts.note: a colonel is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: An eccentric army officer comes across as a bit nutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a nut' suggests mild madness, but means the edible inner part of a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the softer edible seed inside a nutshell.

clue.text: Stop by a windy side street

indicators.note: a windy road twists about, so the letters of side are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone halts beside a winding side street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' twists SIDE into DESI.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something.

clue.text: The Teamsters' strike call to transfer computer data

explanation.surface: A union rallying cry is also a computing instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Teamsters are US truck drivers; a strike call to them would be 'down load!', meaning put down your loads.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking workers lay down their cargo; separately, a computer copies files from a remote server to a local machine.

clue.text: Charming way to write out letters

explanation.surface: There is a charming way to write letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic incantation charms its victim; and to name the letters of a word in order is to give its orthography.

clue.text: Tucking in-to the roast poultry?

parts.note: read as eating heartily, or as tucking a savoury filling into the bird before roasting

explanation.surface: Diners tuck into a roast chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'in-to' gives two readings: gorging yourself, and packing seasoned breadcrumbs into the cavity of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeating and the seasoned filling put inside a roast bird share the same word.

clue.text: Watch a man stuttering

explanation.surface: Someone watches a man who stammers.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiming timepiece that strikes the hours again on demand; and a stammerer says the same sounds over and over.

clue.text: Confessed to being found in possession, but not in bed

parts.note: to have possessed something is to have owned it
someone who is up is out of bed

explanation.surface: A suspect admits guilt after being caught with stolen goods while awake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in possession' sounds like a police charge, but just means owned.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is an idiom for admitting a fault.

clue.text: Called to name the half-way point in a 1000-page novel

parts.note: a novel of this length is made of pages, giving the word page
half of M, the Roman thousand, is D, the Roman five hundred, so the half-way point of the 1000 is D

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to name the middle of a long novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The half-way point of a 1000-page book is page 500, and 500 is D in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To page someone is to summon them by announcement or bleeper.

clue.text: Childhood in the primeval soup

explanation.surface: A childhood spent in primordial ooze.
explanation.definitionFit: One's first years as a child; and the first organisms that arose in the ancient oceans.

clue.text: An electrical unit on the floor of the house?

parts.words: on the floor of the house
parts.note: a Member of Parliament, an MP, speaks on the floor of the House of Commons

explanation.surface: An electrical socket sits on the floor of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks domestic but means the House of Commons, Britain's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the unit of electric current, usually shortened.

clue.text: Apparently they do rest in peace-still

definitions.text: Apparently they do rest in peace

explanation.surface: The departed rest in peace, quite motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically as a description of the deceased lying calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: The deceased lie tranquil; and windless weather at sea is utterly motionless.

clue.text: How well-packed parcels should arrive. Agree?

explanation.surface: Packages should arrive intact, if you agree.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AS SENT: parcels should arrive in the state they were dispatched.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcels should arrive in the same condition as when posted; and to consent is to say yes.

clue.text: Debts covered by rising tides of treason

indicators.note: in a down entry, being covered by a piece means sitting underneath it
in a down entry rising means the word tides is read from bottom to top

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Debts swamped by rising tides sounds like a financial disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns TIDES into SEDIT; 'covered by' places the debts beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious conduct incites rebellion against the state, close to treachery.

clue.text: See lambs gambol and form a flock

indicators.note: lambs gambol by skipping about, so the letters of see and lambs leap into a new order

explanation.surface: Lambs frolic and then gather together as a flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gambol' mixes SEE and LAMBS.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together in one place, as a group of sheep does.

clue.text: What you need if you find nothing in very soft music

indicators.note: in places the letter for nothing inside the musical marking for very soft

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft

explanation.surface: A listener needing quiet music.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is pianissimo in musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for popular music, the chart genre.

clue.text: Welcome mass-immigration policy

explanation.surface: A country welcomes migrants in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: An unobstructed entrance signals hospitality; and a policy of free entry for immigrants or trade is so called.

clue.text: Poem from the works of P.G Wodehouse

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the author's name, as if from within his writings

explanation.surface: A poem by the comic novelist P.G. Wodehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the works of' sends you inside the name: wODEhouse. Wodehouse wrote mostly comic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Slumbering-as the huntsman returns, d'ye ken

indicators.note: returns means the huntsman's name is read backwards

parts.note: John Peel is the huntsman of the old song 'D'ye ken John Peel'

explanation.surface: Asleep as the huntsman comes home, as in the old hunting song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'D'ye ken John Peel' is a Cumbrian hunting song ('do you know John Peel'); 'returns' turns PEEL into LEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slumbering is in a state of sleep.

clue.text: Pea soup for the primate

indicators.note: soup suggests the letters of pea are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: Pea soup served to a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' mixes PEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape is a tailless primate such as a gorilla or chimpanzee.

clue.text: In vain I shall cut down the rogue

indicators.note: In places the shortened form of I shall inside the word vain

parts.note: I shall cut down to a contraction gives I'll

explanation.surface: A threat, perhaps in vain, to cut down a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' looks like violence but means contracted: I shall becomes I'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wicked person or scoundrel.

clue.text: Father fiddles violin where players forgather

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: fiddles means messes about with the letters of violin

explanation.surface: Dad plays the violin where players gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddles' suggests playing the instrument but mixes VIOLIN; the players are cricketers, whose pavilion is their clubhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ground's clubhouse where the teams change and gather.

clue.text: Strive to allot praise

indicators.note: to allot is to distribute or share out, so the letters of praise are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hand out compliments fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allot' shares out PRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim or strive for something ambitious.

clue.text: Would Noah now need it if stranded in Notts?

definitions.text: Would Noah now need it if stranded in Notts?

parts.words: Would Noah now need it if stranded in Notts?
parts.note: split as a fresh vessel for the flood patriarch, and also a market town in Nottinghamshire

explanation.surface: Noah stranded in Nottinghamshire would need a new boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NEW ARK; Newark-on-Trent is a town in Nottinghamshire (Notts), an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh replacement vessel for Noah, and the name of an English market town.

clue.text: A lot of words properly pronounced only by those well versed…

definitions.text: A lot of words properly pronounced only by those well versed…

parts.words: A lot of words properly pronounced only by those well versed…
parts.note: groups of words, but also punishments that may properly be pronounced only by judges, people well versed in the next clue's word

explanation.surface: Many words that only experts can say properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 28-across: those 'well versed in law' are judges, who pronounce prison terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical units of words, and the punishments a judge passes.

clue.text: Half a score or one part of an operatic score

definitions.text: one part of an operatic score

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half of it is ten

explanation.surface: Musings about half of an opera score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' is used twice: first the number twenty, then music.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor is a male voice part in opera and choral music.

clue.text: … and related by marriage

parts.note: completes the previous clue as those well versed in legal matters, and also describes family joined through a wedding

explanation.surface: The run-on ends with relatives by marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with 26-across: 'well versed in law' are judges; alone it means a spouse's relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives acquired through a spouse, such as a mother of one's husband.

clue.text: Desert display of army mourning?

explanation.surface: A deserter and a military display of grief.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A BAND ON: a black band worn on the arm is a mourning sign, hence 'army' (of the arm).
explanation.definitionFit: To forsake or leave behind; and wearing a black armband is a sign of grief.

clue.text: Coffer cacher more likely to catch a cough!

definitions.text: more likely to catch a cough!

explanation.surface: Someone guarding the money is likelier to catch a cough.
explanation.walkthrough: Croup is a childhood cough, so 'croupier' playfully means more croupy; 'Coffer cacher' sounds like 'coffer catcher'.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino employee gathers stakes into the bank; and someone with a worse throat infection is croupier.

clue.text: Maybe one who puts up with an Indian chairman

definitions.text: Maybe one who puts up with

explanation.surface: An Indian chairman who tolerates a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: In colonial India a bearer was a servant who carried a sedan chair; 'chairman' means a chair-carrier, not a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tolerates hardship; and a servant who carries a palanquin in India.
